caption: A pan straight from the stove is set down on a thin plastic cutting board, and the board warps and its edges lift.

sa.check: A pan is set down on a thin plastic cutting board.
The board warps under the pan.
Some of the warp stays after the pan is removed.
The board is flat at the start.
The setting down comes first and the warping follows.

pc.expect: The board is a thin plastic sheet that softens where the pan sits, bends around it and keeps its plastic look.
pc.fail: The board shatters into pieces; or the board runs into a puddle; or the board stays perfectly flat while its edges are plainly lifted; or the board stretches like elastic.

pc.expect: The warp only deepens while the pan sits there and some of it remains after the pan is lifted.
pc.fail: The board springs perfectly flat again the moment the pan is lifted; or the warp deepens and eases in turn; or the board warps before the pan is set down; or the board's edges lift and settle repeatedly with the pan still on it.

pc.expect: The board sags downward where the pan's weight presses and its free edges lift upward off the counter.
pc.fail: The board bulges upward under the pan; or the board's edges curl downward through the counter; or the board lifts off the counter as a whole and hangs; or the pan rises off the board.

pc.expect: The warp forms where the hot pan rests and the board away from it stays flat.
pc.fail: The board warps at a corner the pan never touched; or the pan sits on the board and it stays dead flat to the end of the clip; or the whole board warps evenly while the pan covers one part; or the counter warps rather than the board.

pc.expect: One pan on one board; the board stays one sheet and the pan keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The board splits into separate pieces; or a second board appears; or the pan sinks through the board; or the pan vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The board's colour, the pan's finish and the counter stay the same.
pc.fail: The board changes colour; or the pan changes colour; or items on the counter rearrange.

note: Smoke or smell from the hot plastic is chemistry and is not judged.
